glosses: to convene, convoke (invite together)
to summon, call (call up), invite
to summon; to summons

examples.text: Parce qu’il s’était garé le 11 avril 2019 devant un radar mobile sur la N2 à Remich après s’être fait flasher, un jeune homme de 34 ans était convoqué devant le tribunal correctionnel.
examples.translation: Because he parked in front of a speed camera on the N2 in Remich on 11 April 2019 after being flashed, a 34 year old man was summonsed to court.
examples.english: Because he parked in front of a speed camera on the N2 in Remich on 11 April 2019 after being flashed, a 34 year old man was summonsed to court.

glosses: wezwać, zwołać
Avertir ou ordonner de se réunir.

examples.text: Je suis habitué à ces fantaisies d’officiers. A la caserne, on est fréquemment convoqué par un capitaine inconnu qui veut connaître sans délai l’horaire de paquebots pour la Chine […].
Faire lanterner des heures durant ceux qu’il avait convoqués, déjeuner à pas d’heure ou procéder à une inspection générale d’une caserne en pleine nuit, faisaient partie de ses habitudes.

glosses: Faire appel à, réunir, rassembler.

examples.text: Au loin, les forêts inspiraient des mythologies sombres, les crêtes convoquaient des philosophies tranchées.

glosses: To call people together; to convene; to convoke.

examples.text: Silence is primary, summoning presence to itself; so it's a connection to the realm of origin.

glosses: To ask someone to come; to send for.

examples.text: The cousins separated, and Nain Singh joined a caravan posing as a merchant. This time he crossed the border successfully. Singh eventually entered Jih-k’a-tse, the second-largest city in Tibet. It was in Jih-k’a-tse that he was summoned to meet the country’s second-highest religious authority, the Panchen Lama, who turned out to be only 11 years old.

glosses: To order (goods) and have delivered

examples.text: You can summon groceries, alcohol and medicines to your home: chips and vodka on New Year’s Eve, say, and then aspirin on New Year’s Day.

glosses: To rouse oneself to exert a skill.

examples.text: For securing the attainment of what he considered to be a most desirable end, he summoned all his abilities with a most praiseworthy energy and perseverance.

Joseph needed to summon all his reserve to keep his self-control, for no sooner had Asa voiced his request than Joseph recalled his remark to Aaron about a child being given to this couple in lieu of their giving Mary to him.

November 2 2014, Daniel Taylor, "Sergio Agüero strike wins derby for Manchester City against 10-man United," guardian.co.uk
City will feel nonplussed when they review the tape and Pellegrini had to summon all his restraint in the post-match interviews.

glosses: To call a resource by magic.

examples.text: “Why won't you teach me to summon water? I can summon fire so easily, it's only logical that I should learn to put out my mistakes.”

glosses: To summons; convene.
A creature magically summoned to do the summoner's bidding.

examples.text: Conjuration magic in Baldur's Gate 3 allows players to summon a variety of helpful creatures […] These summons can assist players in combat and exploration, providing strategic advantages with their unique abilities.

glosses: call, command, order

examples.text: The deceased was 58 years of age, was the picture of health even five or six hours prior to his death, when suddenly the grim messenger came with a summon from a Higher Tribunal, calling him to duties above.

glosses: A fine; a fee or monetary penalty incurred for breaking the law; usually for a minor offence such as a traffic violation.

examples.text: You better pay off the parking summon tomorrow before you kena interest on it.

glosses: A notice of an infringement of the law, usually incurring such a penalty; a citation or ticket.
To impose such a fine or penalty, or to issue a notice thereof.

examples.text: The police summoned the driver for speeding.
